chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: Length of engagements, constant work and stranded without pay
summary: They stayed three months a year at the club, worked nearly every night, and once sat idle for six weeks paying their own expenses.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: And how long were you playing at the Cotton Club? In '33?
I don't remember too well. But I think we were there about three months or something -- a couple of

months or something like that. Each year. And the other bands came in. Cab Calloway and finally Jimmie Lunceford and Blue Mills Blue Rhythm Ribbon bands. And all the different bands played the Cotton Club.
All right, you were -- you'd go out on the road in between the Cotton Club engagements.

Oh yes. We'd make the theatrical tour -- all the theaters, and between the theaters you'd make these dance dates. In between that you'd make recordings, and every once in awhile a night club stint. And you stayed busy.
About how many nights a week did the band usually work?

I would say almost every night one way or another. For the first part -- oh let's see -- it must have been the first year or two anyway -- the only time you had any time -- any nights off was usually when you were on the road -- one-nighters. Maybe you'd miss a night here and there.

Then there was a time when there was quite a depression and I remember one time we left New York to play a New Year's Eve dance and we stayed out there not working for about a month and a half.
Out West. Out in the different towns. Because we didn't -- they didn't return you home. They would carry you to that job then you sit there till the next job.
Because you paid your own expenses, see. So there was no ways --
You didn't pay your own travel expense --
No, you paid your own room --
Yeah, room, lodging, food, laundry, and all those kind of expenses.
How far West were you when that happened?
You had to spend a month and a half in Texas --
No, we weren't out that far. It was out in Northeast -- between New York and Chicago I'm pretty sure it was. Pittsburg and places like that.
